$comment: COACH THEM, rebuilt 2026-09-11 as a pool-side lookup, on his ask:
"I want to be able to pull my phone out, read some stuff that will just give me an idea of what to
explain or what to show, because sometimes they're approaching me at the pool."
The version before was four stages of two cues each and a five-line prompt list, and he read it as
four things. Now each item is what he sees, what to say, what to show, and how he knows it worked,
grouped by stroke, fifteen of them.
SOURCES ARE SWIM ENGLAND ONLY, his ruling of 2026-09-02: the two coaching tabs draw on different
families, and Coach me keeps US Masters Swimming. Every item quotes a page captured under
content/swim/sources/, and validate.mjs refuses a quote that is not on that page. Say, show and
watch restate the quoted sentences in fewer words; nothing a quote does not carry is on this tab.
beforeYouStart is his ruling of 2026-09-03 and stays word for word. The history of every earlier
version of this file is in git.

meta.who: Anyone at the pool who asks: complete beginners through to people who swim a bit and want it to feel easier.
meta.sourceFamily: Swim England learn-to-swim and Just Swim pages only.

beforeYouStart.title: Before you take anyone in the water
body: If they cannot float, cannot put their face in, or are frightened, send them to a class. Do it
in shallow water, do not take a nervous person into deep water to demonstrate anything, and do
not hold anyone up. Drowning is quiet and it is fast.
beforeYouStart.$whatChanged: HIS RULING, 2026-09-03: keep all three lines, unchanged. DO NOT ASK AGAIN. The credentials disclaimer went on his ruling of 2026-09-02; the water-safety half stays. The shorten-to-one-line option was offered and not chosen, because it drops "do not hold anyone up", which is the line that stops the helper drowning.

items.see: Nervous, or has never put their face in
items.say: Go at your own pace. Feet first, then a little deeper, then splash your face, then breathe out into the water.
items.show: Standing in water they can stand in: splash the face like washing it, then face in and blow bubbles.
items.watch: They can put the face in and breathe out without grabbing for the side. If they cannot, that is a class, not you.

quotes.text: Start by getting your feet wet and try to gradually get deeper into the water
When you can stand in water deep enough splash water on your face as if you are washing it.
Next try to learn to hold your breath under the water and breathe out into the water. Basically, blow bubbles!
Don't feel rushed to make progress.

items.see: Legs drop the moment they stop moving
items.say: Face in, stretch as long as you can, and let the water hold you up.
items.show: A noodle under the armpits while they get the feel of lying flat.
items.watch: They stay up, stretched out, for a few seconds without kicking or grabbing.

quotes.text: Float on your front with your face in the water, stretching your body as long as possible.
held out in front to use as a float while practicing leg kick, under the armpits as a support when swimming

items.see: Wants to practise just the legs, or just the arms
items.say: Kickboard for the legs. Pull buoy between the thighs for the arms and the breathing.
items.show: Board held out in front, a strong push off the wall, then kick with the body flat at the surface.
items.watch: The body stays flat and at the surface for the whole length.

quotes.text: Simply hold the float out in front of you, with your hands through the two hand holes or gripping over the top of the float. Try to get your body in a horizontal position at the surface of the water. Then begin your leg kick. It is easier if you start with a strong push-off from the wall.

The pull buoy is a figure of eight shaped float, which can be placed between the thighs or ankles to provide support to the body without using the legs. This means that you are free to focus on your arm strokes, whilst also developing upper-body strength.

items.see: Comes up gasping after a few strokes
items.say: Breathe out the whole time your face is in, slowly or all at once. Come up only to breathe in.
items.show: Standing: face in, bubbles out, turn to breathe in. Ten in a row.
items.watch: Bubbles the whole time the face is down. No bubbles means they are still holding it.

quotes.text: Make sure you exhale under the water and try not to hold your breath. It may be a trickle (gentle and continuous) or explosive (all in one go). It can be through your mouth, nose or a combination of the two.
Next try to learn to hold your breath under the water and breathe out into the water. Basically, blow bubbles!

items.see: Lifts the head up and forward to breathe
items.say: Turn your head to the side as your body rolls. Keep one ear in the water.
items.watch: One ear stays in the water through the whole breath.

quotes.text: The head stays in the bow wave, and smoothly turns to one side, not lifting forwards, to inhale as the body rotates.
Try to keep one ear in the water as you turn your head.

items.see: Legs low and dragging, lots of effort
items.say: Legs long, toes pointed, ankles floppy like flippers, and never stop kicking.
items.show: A length on a kickboard, so they feel the kick on its own.
items.watch: The kick runs the whole length, including while the arms pull.

quotes.text: Keep your legs long with toes pointed. Kick your legs up and down (alternating) making your ankles as floppy as possible, using your feet like flippers. Kick your legs fast and continuously.

items.see: A pause with both hands out in front
items.say: Pull all the way to your thigh. As one hand goes in, the other should be leaving at your thigh.
items.watch: Never both hands in front of the head at the same time.

quotes.text: Pull one arm under your body all the way to the thigh.
Keep pulling your arms in a continuous movement so that as one arm enters, the other is ready to exit at the thigh.

items.see: The front hand drops or pulls early while they breathe
items.say: While your head turns, leave the other arm stretched out in front, just under the surface. Face back in before that hand pulls.
items.watch: The front hand stays out in front until the face is back in the water.

quotes.text: As you turn your head, keep your opposite arm extended in front of you and in line with your shoulder. It will be about 20-30 cm under the water with your elbow higher than your wrist. Your wrist higher than your finger tips.
Your face returns to the water before your hand does.

items.see: Fine for one length, wrecked by the second or third
items.say: Breathe every three strokes, decided before you push off, and keep it for the whole length.
items.watch: Count their breaths on two lengths. The same number both times means they are on a rhythm.

quotes.text: The breath cycle is commonly every three or five arm strokes
Try to keep the rhythm of your stroke unaffected by breathing.

items.see: The kick goes nowhere, or the knees come up under the chest
items.say: Heels to your bottom, not knees to your chest. Turn the feet out, push back in a circle, finish with the legs together.
items.watch: The soles face up as the heels come in, and the feet stay turned out on the push, not floppy.

quotes.text: Bring your heels towards your bottom with the soles of your feet facing the ceiling.
Concentrate on bringing your feet to your bottom rather than your knees to your chest.
As your heels come up, turn your feet and knees out and push backwards in a circular motion.
Keep your feet in this flat, turned out position rather than loose.

items.see: Everything happens at once, and there is no glide
items.say: Pull, breathe, kick, glide. Breathe in as the hands come together, then stretch out and glide.
items.watch: After every kick there is a moment stretched out long with the face in.

quotes.text: Lift your head to breathe in as the arms start to come together, stretch your arms out and return your head to the water to breathe out. Breath every stroke: "Pull, Breathe, Kick, Glide".

items.see: The arms sweep all the way back to the hips
items.say: A small circle in front of the shoulders: thumbs down, press out and round, thumbs up, hands together.
items.watch: The hands stay in front of the shoulders the whole time.

quotes.text: Turn your hands so that the thumbs point down with both hands pressing out and round. Turn your hands so the thumbs point up and draw the hands together in a small circular action in front of the shoulders.

items.see: Sitting in the water, hips low, knees breaking the surface
items.say: Ears just in the water, eyes up, stretch long. Knees stay under, toes make a small splash.
items.watch: The knees stay under the surface and the splash is at the toes.

quotes.text: Float on your back, with your ears just in the water and eyes looking up; stretch your body as long as possible.
Keep knees under the water with your toes making a small splash.

items.see: Bent arms over the water, or the hand slaps in thumb first
items.say: A straight arm over the top, and the little finger goes in first.
items.watch: The little finger enters first and the arm is straight as it comes over.

quotes.text: Your arm should be kept straight bringing it out of the water over the top in an arc action. Enter your hands into the water with your little fingers first, keeping your arm straight.
Your little finger will enter the water first with your palm facing outwards.

items.see: The arms windmill round without moving them anywhere
items.say: Under the water, bend the arm and push the water towards your feet, finishing at the thigh.
items.watch: The hand finishes down by the thigh on every stroke.

quotes.text: Your arm will start to bend so that the palm and forearm are facing towards your feet. When the elbow gets to a 90 degree bend, push the water towards your hip.
Pull your arm under the water all the way to the thigh.
